edges.description: Retained acid with preserved chloride handling gives an acidosis with a normal anion gap.
Impaired distal proton secretion increases the electrochemical drive for potassium secretion in the same nephron segment.
Acidosis mobilises bone buffer, raising the filtered calcium load, and increases proximal citrate reabsorption, lowering the urinary citrate that would otherwise hold that calcium in solution.
Chronic buffering of retained acid at the expense of bone mineral.
The wasting is the mechanism; the low plasma potassium is the measured phenotype.
Calcium salts precipitate in the medullary interstitium once urinary solubility is exceeded.
The same supersaturation forms discrete stones as well as diffuse medullary deposition.
Calcification and stone disease damage the interstitium over years, which is how the renal arm reaches chronic kidney disease.
Cumulative nephron loss presenting as reduced glomerular filtration rate.
The systemic growth consequence of sustained acidosis and its skeletal buffering.
Demineralisation at the growth plate, the radiographic form the bone lesion takes in the growing skeleton.

Endolymphatic compartment enlargement accompanies the pump defect. The edge is drawn with unknown intermediates on purpose - the mouse shows enlarged endolymphatic compartments in a V-ATPase mutant, but nothing establishes the steps between failed proton secretion and the structural change, and in humans the association is with dRTA generally rather than with this gene.
Failure of endolymph homeostasis in the cochlea, with loss of the endocochlear potential that drives hair cell transduction.

edges.description: The null abolishes the endocochlear potential, which is the direct physiological readout of endolymph homeostasis failure.
edges.limitations: The human auditory phenotype is variable in onset and sometimes absent, whereas the null mouse is uniformly and severely affected. The model therefore describes the mechanism faithfully while overstating its penetrance, so it cannot be used to reason about which ATP6V0A4 patients will lose hearing.

edges.description: Severe metabolic acidosis with hypokalaemia by weaning, lethal without alkali, matching the untreated human course.
The null reproduces the hypocitraturia but not the hypercalciuria, so it dissociates the two halves of this node rather than reproducing it whole.
edges.limitations: Hypercalciuria is absent in the mouse and present in most human patients. Inferences from this model about calcium handling or stone risk in the human disease therefore do not hold, even though the model does develop nephrocalcinosis.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss of function in the a4 subunit of the V0 membrane domain of the vacuolar H+-ATPase. Like the B1 subunit, a4 has expression largely restricted to kidney and inner ear, which is why losing it produces a two-organ disease rather than the systemic failure a housekeeping pump subunit would cause.

evidence.snippet: Recently, we identified mutations in genes encoding two different subunits of the renal alpha-intercalated cell's apical H(+)-ATPase that cause rdRTA.

evidence.reference_title: A gain-of-function mutation in ATP6V0A4 drives primary distal renal tubular alkalosis with enhanced V-ATPase activity.
evidence.snippet: Previous studies have suggested that mutations in ATP6V0A4 consistently result in a loss of function, impairing the hydrogen ion transport efficacy of V-ATPase and leading to distal renal tubular acidosis and sensorineural hearing loss.

genetic_context.description: Biallelic loss of function, most series reporting homozygous variants in consanguineous kindreds and compound heterozygosity elsewhere. The loss-of-function direction is not an assumption here - it is what separates this disease from the alkalosis phenotype produced by a gain-of-function variant in the same gene.

nodes.description: A germline null that reproduces both arms of the human disease. It is the model that turns the auditory arm from an expression-and-inference argument into a measured one, and it also shows an extrarenal, extra-auditory phenotype - impaired olfaction - that has no established human counterpart.

evidence.reference_title: Atp6v0a4 knockout mouse is a model of distal renal tubular acidosis with hearing loss, with additional extrarenal phenotype.
evidence.snippet: This mouse model recapitulates the loss of H(+)-ATPase function seen in human disease and can provide additional insights into dRTA and the physiology of the a4 subunit.

nodes.description: GeneReviews lists potassium-sparing diuretics among the agents to use with caution or avoid. This is counterintuitive, because the disease runs with hypokalaemia and a potassium-sparing agent looks corrective - but these drugs act on the same distal segment whose proton secretion is already failing, so the acidosis is worsened while the potassium is being chased.

evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Potassium-sparing diuretics should be used with caution or avoided.

nodes.description: Declining glomerular filtration, present in about a third of children and the large majority of adults with dRTA. It is the outcome that makes the renal arm of this disease consequential beyond the electrolyte disturbance, and the reason surveillance is lifelong.

evidence.snippet: Renal complications of hereditary dRTA include nephrocalcinosis, nephrolithiasis, medullary cysts, and impaired kidney function.

nodes.description: Loss of the same proton pump in the inner ear, where it contributes to the acid-base composition of endolymph. In the mouse null the consequence is unambiguous, and it is the strongest mechanistic evidence available for this arm: the endocochlear potential is not merely reduced but absent. In humans the arm is variable, and when it manifests is the least settled question in this disease.

nodes.description: The pump cannot move protons across the apical membrane into the tubular lumen or, in the inner ear, into the endolymphatic compartment. This one failed transport step is the branch point of the entry: the renal and the auditory consequences both hang off it, and neither is downstream of the other. That architecture is what makes alkali therapy ineffective for the hearing loss.

nodes.description:
Amplification, escalating to cochlear implantation as the hearing loss progresses. It is curated as a separate treatment from alkali because it addresses the other arm of the disease: the auditory branch is parallel to the acidosis, so correcting blood pH does nothing for it and the only available intervention is to compensate for the deficit.
This record is the reason the two-armed architecture is not merely a modelling preference. If the arms were in series, treating the acidosis early would be an ear treatment too, and it is not.

The stone-forming combination: more calcium in the urine and less of the citrate that keeps it soluble. Notably the mouse null for this gene is hypocitraturic without being hypercalciuric, so the two halves of this node are not obligately linked.

nodes.description: The kidney cannot excrete the daily acid load or regenerate the bicarbonate consumed in buffering it. The diagnostic signature is a urine that stays inappropriately alkaline while the blood is acidotic. No ontology descriptor is bound to this node - see notes.

evidence.snippet: Primary distal renal acidosis (dRTA) is characterized by hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis due to failure in proton excretion, variably severe nephrocalcinosis and/or nephrolithiasis associated with hypercalciuria and hypocitraturia.

nodes.description:
Bicarbonate and citrate salts given to replace the buffer the kidney cannot regenerate. Citrate preparations do double duty, since urinary citrate is itself the depleted inhibitor of calcium precipitation in this disease.
It treats the consequence and not the cause. The pump stays defective and the urine stays inappropriately alkaline. Critically, it does not act on the ear: the auditory arm is parallel to the acidosis rather than downstream of it, so correcting blood pH has no mechanistic reason to change hearing outcome.

evidence.reference_title: [Primary distal renal tubular acidosis].
evidence.snippet: The medical treatment is simple and involves an alkali load which allows curing the metabolic acidosis.

evidence.reference_title: [Primary distal renal tubular acidosis].
evidence.snippet: Long-term outcome is usually good unless the patient's compliance is low or alkalizing treatment is insufficient.

nodes.description: Sustained medullary calcification and stone disease scar the interstitium, and renal function declines over time. This is the node the renal arm was missing - nephrocalcinosis is not an endpoint, it is the step by which a treatable electrolyte disorder becomes chronic kidney disease, and it is the reason the surveillance schedule exists.

evidence.snippet: There was an increased prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) Stage >=2 in children (35%) and adults (82%).

nodes.description:
A prolonged-release combination developed specifically for dRTA, addressing the thing that determines outcome in this disease - adherence to a frequently dosed, unpalatable alkali. Over 24 months it held plasma bicarbonate and potassium in range in most patients, and spine bone mineral density z-score rose.
Best read as a better treatment of the acidosis rather than a treatment of the disease. It acts on the same node the older alkali salts do; nothing in the reported outcomes bears on the auditory arm.

nodes.description: Continued distal potassium secretion in the face of failed proton secretion, giving hypokalaemia that is occasionally severe enough to present as paralysis before the acidosis is recognised.
Demineralisation at the growth plate from chronic buffering of retained acid by bone. The adult counterpart is osteomalacia.

nodes.description: The variable feature the disease name encodes. Originally described as preserved hearing or hearing loss beginning in young adulthood, then shown to begin as early as two months of age in some patients. Onset, not presence, is what distinguishes this from the ATP6V1B1 form.

evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, seven probands with ATP6V0A4 gene mutations developed severe early SNHL between the ages of 2 mo and 10 yr.

nodes.description: Bone as the acid buffer of last resort. Chronic mineral release impairs bone physiology in the growing skeleton and produces the growth failure that brings many of these children to attention in the first place.
